key_insight: UniD shows that a single video model can learn multiple dense scene properties from disjoint, imperfectly labeled datasets instead of requiring one fully annotated dataset. This makes unified scene understanding more practical and scalable.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the fragmentation of dense video annotation: depth, normals, semantics, and other scene labels are spread across incompatible datasets, making unified training difficult. It also avoids the high cost of generating pseudo-labels for missing annotations.
method: Trains one unified video model to predict eight dense scene properties jointly.
Uses disjoint data rather than requiring fully co-annotated samples.
Reduces reliance on expensive pseudo-labeling by learning across heterogeneous annotation sources.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this lowers the barrier to building multi-task video understanding systems from real-world datasets that are rarely fully labeled. It can reduce annotation costs and improve deployment of unified perception models.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing multiple disjoint datasets feeding one unified model

paper_title: Unified Video Dense Prediction from Disjoint Data
paper_authors: Yihong Sun, Seoung Wug Oh, Jiahui Huang, Bharath Hariharan, Joon-Young Lee
